findings: PLUNK SOURCE 1 - the enemy does not budge. FETCH's skull-contact block (C:/Users/Alex/Projects/fetch-claude/src/enemies.js:235-249) flips e.state to 'stunned' and starts a convulsion sine (rotation.z wobble + color dimming, lines 193-196) but applies zero positional displacement, zero impact-frame pose (no head snap, no rock-back), and no reaction scaled to skull speed. KICK BALL names this exact failure in its own comment (game/game.js:5086-5087): 'Getting hit visibly moves it. A creature that takes damage without budging is the main reason a hit reads as nothing happened.'

PLUNK SOURCE 2 - the skull has no carom. On hit, enemies.js:241/247 calls skull.beginReturn('hit'); returning mode (skull.js:687-707) lerps velocity toward the cradle at returnBendRate 9, so the frames right after contact show the skull smoothly curving home with most of its forward velocity intact - there is no direction-change spike at the moment of contact. KICK BALL reflects the ball off the creature first (game.js:5075-5078: velocity.addScaledVector(normal, -1.25*along)) and only then lets the return law bend it home, so contact is visible in the trajectory itself.

PLUNK SOURCE 3 - the impact vocabulary port is hollow. FETCH's game.impact() (main.js:274-278) is a stripped copy of KICK BALL's impact() (game.js:5976-6027, 'THE IMPACT LANGUAGE'): it kept hitStop+shake but dropped every other layer - the white bloom particle bursts, the expanding pulse ring (outward=hurt, inward=locked), the hit marker, and the material-scaled audio call. Time stutters but nothing blooms at the contact point.

PLUNK SOURCE 4 - flat, wrong-family audio. The stun sound is audio.thud (audio.js:806-822), a 120->38Hz sine + lowpassed noise, called at FIXED rate 0.7 and gain 0.8 (enemies.js:246) regardless of skull speed. The same thud recipe serves wall/floor bounces (skull.js:843), so hitting a BODY sounds like hitting the FLOOR, only slower. No sharp transient (compare pop's highpassed crack layer, audio.js:858-863), no speed scaling (compare KICK BALL audio.impact, game.js:939-955, where freq=76+value*45 and gain scale with strength, and bounce strength = |velocity along normal|/38 at game.js:4745), and the enemy's own presence loop keeps droning unchanged through the hit - the creature's voice never reacts.

PLUNK SOURCE 5 - the kill is not temporally bigger than the stun. _pop (enemies.js:279-289) uses the same impact('break') 0.085s hit-stop as a stun, then removes the mesh THE SAME FRAME (line 284 via _remove); only gore chunks remain, and they are near-black 0x1a1216 icosahedrons (main.js:280-290) that barely read in a dark game. PARTY ANIMAL tiers its stops - touch 0.045s, kill 0.085s, boss kill 0.22s (party_animal_2.html:748,782) - and KICK BALL gives corpses a 0.82s physical death: launched away+up (10 lateral, 8 up), tumbling rotation, shrinking scale (game.js:5100-5101, 5608-5618).

PLUNK SOURCE 6 - camera response is translate-only and the freeze is a total hitch. FETCH shake is a CSS translate of the canvas (main.js:484-488) with no rotational component and no FOV response; during hitStop the loop only re-renders the identical frame (main.js:501). KICK BALL applies shake INTO camera rotation (pitch/yaw offsets, shake^2 magnitude, decay 2.8/s, game.js:4012-4021), damps FOV toward base+speed/action (4022-4024), and during hit-stop still advances the camera at dt*0.18 (game.js:3850-3856) so the freeze feels like impact, not a dropped frame. PARTY ANIMAL likewise keeps shake decaying during stopT (party_animal_2.html:2538-2546).

PLUNK SOURCE 7 - the weapon never celebrates. skull.grab() (skull.js:407-419) has the full confirm package for FETCH quests: snap-shut jaw, 0.45s flourish spin + scale swell (_flourishT, skull.js:746-753), tooth CLACK + bright chime. Combat hits trigger none of it - the skull that just cracked a walker's ribs shows nothing. PARTY ANIMAL's equivalent confirm layers on every melee hit: attacker lunges 18px into the swing (tryMelee, party_animal_2.html:765-766), combo-pitched tom on a MIDI ladder quantized to the music grid (AU.tom, 323-336), confetti, popText.

PARTY ANIMAL's full melee hit recipe for reference (party_animal_2.html tryMelee 763-790 + killEnemy 740-761): attacker lunge 18px; enemy shoved 16px along hit angle; hitFlash 0.14s rendered as body fill going WHITE (brightness, not hue - line 1795,1808); stopT 0.045 hit / 0.085 kill; shake 3 hit / 7 kill; 8 confetti hit / 26 kill; permanent floor stain (stampFloor 702-722); pitch-ladder tom per combo; kill = crash cymbal (highpass 5200 noise 0.9s + 190->44Hz boom sine, 337-354); whiff gets its own whoosh (789, 355-366). Player hurt makes the whole MIX flinch: master lowpass dives to 820Hz in 30ms and recovers over 0.55s (404-420).

KICK BALL's hit-stop input law (game.js:3848-3856): edge inputs are captured BEFORE the hit-stop early-return so taps never vanish inside impact frames. FETCH's main loop already honors this ('edges buffered, not lost', main.js:501) - the fixed-step loop needs no change for any of the proposals below.

Economy check: FETCH's stun currently borrows the LOUD tier (impact 'break' = 0.085s stop + 0.46 shake) while pop gets the identical tier. The quiet/loud economy (stun=quiet, pop=LOUD) should be expressed in TIME as well as volume: stun belongs at the 'hurt' tier (0.05s), pop should own the biggest stop in the game (~0.13s) plus the duck it already has (audio.js:871). KICK BALL states the principle at game.js:5985-5987: 'The load-bearing distinction is time: if the game stutters, you hurt it.'

Constraint audit of everything proposed: nothing touches the 0.6s iframes (enemies.js:234-238), the throw grammar, FEEL_PROFILE, or the fixed-step loop; all visual cues are brightness/motion/scale (colorblind-safe); nothing adds HUD; every technique has an audio-first expression; knockback displacement must route through the existing _moveWithPush (enemies.js:330-345) so shoved enemies cannot tunnel through walls.

In the 'stunned' case (lines 191-204), integrate e.knockV through _moveWithPush with exponential decay (multiplyScalar(exp(-6*dt))) so the creature ROCKS back ~0.5-1.0m and catches itself, and add a one-shot recoil pose: mesh rotation.x snaps to -0.3 in the first 0.1s of stunT then damps back to the convulsion. Horror-tuned: it staggers and recovers, it does not fly. iframes and stun duration untouched.

summary: FETCH's 'plunk' is precisely diagnosable: the enemy takes a hit without budging (state flip only, no displacement or recoil pose), the skull curves smoothly home with no carom off the body, main.js impact() is a hollowed port of KICK BALL's impact language (time+shake kept, bloom/ring/marker/audio-scaling dropped), the stun sound is the same thud family as wall bounces at a fixed rate with no transient or speed scaling and no reaction from the enemy's voice loop, the pop despawns the corpse the same frame with the SAME hit-stop as a stun, and the camera answer is translate-only CSS shake with a dead-frame freeze. Eleven portable techniques from PARTY ANIMAL and KICK BALL fix this within FETCH's constraints - stagger knockback via _moveWithPush, a pre-return velocity carom, completing the impact vocabulary with a dim bloom + ring (plus an inward 'locked' ring for the unkillables), retiering hit-stop so the pop owns the longest stop, cosmetic-only camera drift during freezes, small rotational shake + FOV punch, velocity-scaled thud with a bone-crack transient, a presence-loop choke so the creature's drone gasps when struck, reusing the existing grab-flourish/tooth-CLACK as the combat confirm, and a 0.6s tumbling corpse with a permanent floor stain. None touch FEEL_PROFILE, the throw grammar, the fixed-step loop, or the 0.6s iframes; every cue is brightness/motion/audio, never hue, never HUD.
